notes:
Account summary
- Polaris Support Platform is a customer support automation SaaS (agentic chat + ticket summarization + knowledge base retrieval). They’re evaluating Redwood after reading the public benchmark report; they keep coming back to two themes: (1) p95 latency under real concurrency and (2) streaming stability (smooth token cadence, no stalls/timeouts).

Primary use case / workload details (from discovery)
- Frontend: end-user chat widget embedded in customers’ help centers; streaming responses are required (UX is tuned for ‘fast first token’).
- Backend: RAG over customer KB + conversation history; occasional tool/function calls (ticket creation, CRM lookups).
- Mix: ~70% short chats (200–600 output tokens), ~25% longer ‘troubleshooting’ chats (800–1500 output tokens), ~5% heavy summarization jobs (2k–4k output tokens) executed asynchronously.
- Concurrency: peaks during business hours; they estimate 120–250 concurrent chats at peak for the pilot, with spikes during incidents/outages.

Key requirements called out (verbatim-ish)
- “We get yelled at for p95, not p50.” They want p95 end-to-end to stay tight under bursty load; asked specifically how Redwood handles queueing and whether p95 is dominated by ‘cold’ requests.
- Streaming: they’re sensitive to stalls (multi-second pauses) more than raw tokens/sec. They asked how Redwood surfaces stream interruptions and whether SDK retries can duplicate partial output.
- Regions: initial pilot is NA-only (us-east + us-west). Longer-term they expect EU expansion and want to avoid re-architecting.

What they liked
- Benchmark framing (latency/$) resonated, but they’re not optimizing purely for cost; they want predictable latency first, then cost control.
- They appreciated that methodology/disclaimers are published and that Redwood is willing to share configs/manifests conceptually (they asked for ‘how to replicate’ guidance).

Concerns / objections
- Variance: Polaris had prior issues with another provider where p95 degraded significantly during shared-capacity contention. They asked whether Hosted API is multi-tenant and what Dedicated buys them in measurable p95 terms.
- Streaming reliability: they had an incident with their current provider where streaming connections dropped under load; they want to understand Redwood’s recommended client timeouts, retry/backoff, and whether partial streams are resumable.
- Support ticket context: they referenced seeing community chatter about launch-week benchmark landing page issues (asked ‘was that a sign of reliability issues?’). We clarified that was web page caching/CDN, not inference plane, but they want confidence we isolate marketing traffic from serving.

Positioning / product fit (internal)
- Recommended path: start Hosted API for 1–2 week PoC (their prompt set + their concurrency profile), then propose Dedicated for production if p95 targets require isolation/predictability.
- Potential attach: Optimize for batching/caching guidance once workload is characterized; they’re very open to prescriptive knobs as long as quality is stable.

Open questions to resolve in technical deep dive
- Exact SLO targets: first token p95 target and steady-state token cadence expectations (they used the phrase ‘no more than ~500–800ms dead air after first token’).
- Their timeout/retry policy today and what failures are most painful (HTTP timeouts vs stream disconnects vs slow starts).
- Model preferences: they are currently split across 2 models (one cheaper for simple deflection, one stronger for complex cases). They asked if Redwood can route by policy and provide fallback if capacity is constrained.

Next step (confirmed)
- 60-min technical deep dive with Markus + Stephanie + Polaris Eng lead/SRE. Agenda: (1) how we measure/monitor p95, (2) streaming behavior and recommended client configs, (3) Dedicated sizing & isolation model, (4) PoC plan + success criteria and how to report results.

Internal notes
- If they push hard on p95 predictability: bring in Reliability/SRE talking points (variance/stability gates, repeat-run methodology), and be explicit about what Dedicated SLAs can cover vs what depends on client/network.
- Consider offering a structured PoC harness: their prompts + concurrency sweep (50/100/200) + streaming cadence metrics; align on reporting format so it’s not ‘vibes’.
